findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 25-26 May publication draft
findings.headline: Whistleblowing case identified areas requiring governance improvement
findings.detail: One whistleblowing case was reported during 2025/26. When considered by the Audit Committee in March 2026, 'an action plan approved to address areas where improvement is needed'. This suggests the whistleblowing governance process or investigation had gaps requiring remediation.
findings.matters: Whistleblowing governance weaknesses suggest potential issues with how misconduct and fraud concerns are being surfaced and handled; this affects fraud risk management.
findings.figures: One whistleblowing case reported in 2025/26
findings.quote: the outcome of the only case reported under the policy in the financial year was considered by the Committee in March 2026, with an action plan approved to address areas where improvement is needed.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 25-26 May publication draft
findings.headline: Senior Leadership Team restructured July 2025 with formal governance action to ensure capacity during Local Government Reorganisation
findings.detail: Hart restructured its Senior Leadership Team in July 2025 with 'residual capacity assessed and deputy arrangements put in place'. A governance improvement action has been added specifically 'in light of LGR and the SLT restructure in July 2025, ensure effective leadership and management capacity across the council's services' due throughout 2026/27.
findings.matters: Leadership capacity and continuity directly affect decision-making quality and service delivery; LGR creates additional organizational demands during a leadership transition, and capacity constraints could affect council stability.
findings.figures: SLT restructured July 2025; improvement action due throughout 2026/27
findings.quote: The Senior Leadership Team was restructured in July 2025 with residual capacity assessed and deputy arrangements put in place.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 25-26 May publication draft
findings.headline: Internal Audit management action recommendations not being implemented within agreed timescales
findings.detail: The Audit Committee noted in March 2026 that management is not consistently implementing internal audit recommendations by the timescales they have agreed to. This has been identified as a governance improvement issue requiring managers to 'better assess realistic deadlines when they agree and sign off the management actions in IA reports'.
findings.matters: Failure to implement audit recommendations on time indicates weak management discipline and suggests identified control weaknesses are not being fixed, which increases underlying control risk.
findings.figures: Issue noted Audit Committee March 2026; improvement actions due throughout 2026/27
findings.quote: Internal audits management actions are not all being implemented within agreed timescales, as noted by Audit Committee in March 2026

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 25-26 May publication draft
findings.headline: Finance system implementation ongoing with final phases and AI module due December 2026
findings.detail: Hart implemented a new financial system during 2025/26. Internal Audit has reviewed key aspects with positive outcomes reported. However, governance improvement action plan identifies that 'final phases, including AI module, are completed on time and on budget with robust controls across all modules' as a priority with December 2026 completion target, indicating implementation is not yet complete.
findings.matters: Incomplete finance system implementation with major modules still pending creates risk to financial reporting accuracy and timeliness; major modules like an AI component add complexity to controls.
findings.figures: New system implemented 2025/26; final phases and AI module due Dec 2026
findings.quote: A new financial system was implemented during 2025/26, key aspects of which have been subject to assurance reviews by Internal Audit, with positive outcomes reported.

findings.paper_title: Annual Governance Statement 25-26 May publication draft
findings.headline: External auditors gave a qualified audit opinion on 2024/25 accounts
findings.detail: EY completed Hart's 2024/25 accounts audit on a 'qualified' basis due to the government's reset approach to clear backlogs. Despite the qualified opinion, EY's Value for Money conclusion was positive, finding the Council has proper arrangements to plan and manage resources, make informed decisions, and manage risks.
findings.matters: A qualified audit opinion is a material concern for lenders and indicates auditor reservations about the accounts or control environment; understanding the nature of the qualification is essential for credit decisions.
findings.figures: 2024/25 audit completed on qualified basis; EY Value for Money conclusion positive
findings.quote: The external Auditors, EY, have now concluded their 2024/25 accounts audit, although it was completed on a 'qualified' audit basis due to the ongoing impact of the government's 'reset' approach to clear backlogs.

findings.headline: No value-for-money significant weaknesses identified, but auditor notes ongoing need for governance improvements on cyber security and risk register timeliness
findings.detail: The auditor confirmed no significant weaknesses in arrangements for financial sustainability, governance, or improving economy, efficiency and effectiveness. However, the Annual Governance Statement discloses ongoing improvements needed: 'timely completion of audits due to sector-wide resource constraints, enhancement of risk registers to reflect emerging financial and operational risks and strengthening cyber security controls in line with national guidance.'
findings.matters: While the clean VFM conclusion is positive, the disclosed gaps in cyber security and risk register timeliness are emerging governance risks. Cyber incidents or unidentified financial risks could crystallise quickly.
findings.figures: Four Audit Committee meetings held in 2024/25; no outstanding VFM recommendations from prior years
findings.quote: However, areas for improvement disclosed in the AGS include timely completion of audits due to sector-wide resource constraints, enhancement of risk registers to reflect emerging financial and operational risks and strengthening cyber security controls in line with national guidance.

findings.headline: Pension liability disclosure error of £764k in fair value of pension assets, though no impact on reported liability
findings.detail: The auditor identified a £764k misstatement in disclosures relating to the closing fair value of pension assets and asset ceiling effect. Although this had no impact on the reported pension liability in the accounts, it suggests a gap in the quality of pension accounting data preparation.
findings.matters: Pension liabilities are often a council's largest off-balance-sheet exposure. Disclosure errors signal weak internal controls over actuarial data reconciliation, which could mask larger errors in the liability valuation itself.
findings.figures: £764k misstatement in pension asset fair value disclosure
findings.quote: As part of our testing, we identified one misstatement in the disclosures relating to the closing fair value of pension assets and asset ceiling effect, amounting to £764k but this has no impact on the reported pension liability in the accounts.

findings.headline: Serco waste contract extended for 8 years from October 2025, but new government waste legislation creates contract performance uncertainty
findings.detail: The council and partner Basingstoke & Deane Borough Council have agreed an 8-year extension with Serco from 1 October 2025. The original main contract was due to end mid-2026. However, the auditor notes: 'due to new government legislation, there is uncertainty on waste services moving forward' and this has been flagged in the council's risk register. The extended contract represents a major fixed cost commitment in an environment of legislative flux.
findings.matters: Waste services are a material council cost. An 8-year commitment to Serco locks the council into a single provider and cost structure during a period when central government is reshaping waste policy (e.g., Extended Producer Responsibility). Changes to waste legislation could create unfunded burdens or stranded contract costs.
findings.figures: 8-year contract extension from 1 October 2025; original contract end date was mid-2026
findings.quote: The main contract with Serco is due to end midway through 2026, and due to new government legislation, there is uncertainty on waste services moving forward. This has been identified in their Risk Register as discussed earlier in this document, with The Council, in partnership with Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council, has agreed an 8-year extension with Serco from 1 Oct 2025.

findings.headline: Reliance on sustained savings delivery to balance budget: £2.1m in 2024/25, £1.2m planned for 2025/26
findings.detail: The council balanced its 2025/26 budget through application of £6.5m of savings and mitigations without drawing unallocated reserves. This follows delivery of £2.1m savings in 2024/25. The 2025/26 savings target of £1.274m is dependent on identified measures: food waste funding (£0.8m), 2.99% council tax (£0.3m), and senior leadership vacancy management (£0.15m), with a gap of £1.2m still to be identified.
findings.matters: Councils that rely on continuous savings programmes risk service quality degradation and stumbling if headcount reductions or income measures hit implementation obstacles. Hart's track record of delivery is solid, but the forward gap of £1.2m in 2025/26 is not yet closed.
findings.figures: £2.1m savings delivered 2024/25; £1.274m target for 2025/26; £1.2m of 2025/26 target still to be identified
findings.quote: The 2025/26 Budget has been balanced through the application of £6.5 million of savings and mitigations, without the need to drawdown from unallocated reserves.

findings.headline: Treasury income pressure of up to £150k annually from expected interest rate changes
findings.detail: The council's MTFS identifies a forecast reduction in treasury investment returns due to expected interest rate changes, with budgeted pressure of £150k in 2026/27 and £100k in 2028/29. This reflects the impact of holding £42.1m in investments at lower yields as rates fall, creating a structural income headwind.
findings.matters: Treasury income has been a material positive contributor to the council's financial position (£715k gain in 2024/25). Future reliance on investment returns is now at risk, removing a buffer that has helped absorb other pressures.
findings.figures: £42.1m total investments held; treasury income pressure of £150k (2026/27) and £100k (2028/29) forecast
findings.quote: Key challenges for 2025/26 include inflationary impacts on service costs, increased employer National Insurance contributions of approximately £300k, and new obligations such as the rollout of food waste collection and preparation for potential local government reorganisation, forecast reduction in treasury investment returns due to expected interest rate changes, adding £150k pressure in 2026/27 and £100k in 2028/29.

findings.headline: Investment property valuation overstatement of £1.244m identified and corrected in audit
findings.detail: During audit testing of a sample of investment properties, the auditor identified one property with an overstatement in valuation requiring a £1.244m correction, which management agreed. While the auditor concluded this does not indicate a material weakness in controls, it demonstrates a valuation quality control gap on a significant asset class.
findings.matters: Investment properties are material to balance sheet presentation and fund availability. A £1.2m error that survived internal review before audit suggests control gaps in asset valuation governance.
findings.figures: £1.244m overstatement correction on investment property
findings.quote: As part of our testing, we identified one audit difference within the sample of properties reviewed. The audit difference related to an overstatement in valuation and required a correction of £1,244k which has been agreed by the management.

findings.headline: Structural funding gap of £2.4m forecast for 2026/27–2028/29 despite delivering savings
findings.detail: The council's Medium-Term Financial Strategy projects a structural funding gap even after applying annual council tax increases at 2.99% and implementing savings. The gaps are £1.4m (2026/27), £0.6m (2027/28), and £0.4m (2028/29), totalling £2.4m. Drivers include inflationary cost pressures, increased employer National Insurance contributions (~£300k), treasury investment return reductions (£150k in 2026/27, £100k in 2028/29), and new statutory burdens such as food waste collection and local government reorganisation preparation.
findings.matters: A structural gap of this size, persisting across the medium term, signals that the council cannot rely on one-off savings or reserves to balance its budget sustainably. This requires meaningful service change or further income generation.
findings.figures: Cumulative shortfall of £2.4m over 2026/27–2028/29; 2.99% council tax rise generates additional £254k in 2025/26, rising to £280k by 2028/29
findings.quote: The MTFS projects a structural funding gap from 2026/27 onwards, even after applying annual council tax increases of 2.99%. The residual gaps are £1.4m in 2026/27, £0.6m in 2027/28, and £0.4m in 2028/29. This results in a cumulative shortfall of £2.4m over the period.

findings.headline: Qualified opinion on financial statements with multi-year assurance gaps on historical property valuations
findings.detail: The auditor issued a qualified opinion on 2024/25 accounts (progress from prior-year disclaimers on 2023/24 and 2022/23). However, due to gaps in assurance over Property, Plant and Equipment valued in 2022/23, the auditor cannot verify all opening balances, in-year movements, and 2024/25 comparative balances. The auditor states: 'we do not have assurance over some brought forward balances from 2023/24 where we did not gain assurance (the opening balances). This means we do not have assurance over all 2024/25 in-year movements and the comparative prior year movements.'
findings.matters: A lender needs confidence in the reliability of financial statements. Unresolved audit gaps on asset valuations and opening balances limit confidence in reported position and comparability across years.
findings.figures: PPE valuation issues from 2022/23 remain unresolved; forecast to move to unqualified opinion by 2026/27 per LARRIG01 recovery plan
findings.quote: Although the level of assurance gained has increased, we have not yet obtained sufficient evidence to have reasonable assurance over all in-year movements and closing balances.

findings.headline: Capital spending £3.5m under budget (42% underspend), driven by supplier resource issues and project approval delays
findings.detail: Capital forecast £4.9m against £8.4m budget. Delays include Edenbrook car park (supplier resourcing problems), Frogmore heat pump (Cabinet approval delayed to January 2026), and cascade delays on solar and insulation schemes. The scale of underspend suggests execution challenges.
findings.matters: Large capital underspends and delays indicate delivery risk and reduce planned service improvements or efficiency gains; concentrated carry-forwards into 26/27 increase next year's execution pressure
findings.figures: £3.5m underspend on £8.4m budget; Edenbrook £144k carry forward; Frogmore heat pump £1,159k carry forward
findings.quote: Capital projects are forecast to be £3.5m less than budget, mainly due to rescheduling into 26/27. The external supplier selected to deliver this project has experienced resourcing problems.

findings.headline: Income forecast revised down £202k from Q2, with planning development, building control, and grants all underperforming
findings.detail: Three income streams were revised downward from Q2: planning development -£80k, building control -£40k, grants -£78k. While the Q3 outturn remains positive overall, these downward revisions indicate income is not tracking expectations and future income reliability is uncertain.
findings.matters: Lenders depend on stable, predictable income to support debt servicing; repeated downward forecast revisions create uncertainty for future cash flow
findings.figures: Planning development -£80k, building control -£40k, grants -£78k; total -£202k
findings.quote: Income: -£202k : Planning development -£80k, building control -£40k, grants -£78k

findings.headline: Council deliberately depleting reserves to maintain £25.9m under-borrowed position, betting on interest rates to fall by mid-2027.
findings.detail: Hart is not undertaking new borrowing despite a capital financing requirement of £39.9m (2024/25), instead funding capital expenditure from capital receipts, grants, and reserves. The paper explicitly describes this as deliberate: reserves are being used 'as a temporary measure' while awaiting interest rate falls. Treasury advisors (MUFG) forecast Bank Rate to fall to 3.25% by Q3 2027 and PWLB 5-year certainty rates to fall from current 4.78% to 4.20% by Q2 2027. As a result, fund balances are declining from £53.2m (2024/25) to £38.1m (2028/29) — a £15.1m reduction over four years. Zero borrowing is planned for any year through 2028/29.
findings.matters: Lenders need to understand refinancing risk. The strategy depends entirely on specific interest rate forecasts. If rates don't fall as expected, the council will face higher borrowing costs when it eventually refinances, and reserve depletion limits flexibility for unexpected costs.
findings.figures: Under-borrowing £25,885k (2024/25); fund balances declining £53,166k to £38,097k; external debt £14,079k (31/03/2025) declining to £13,624k (30/11/2025); borrowing requirement £0 for 2026/27–2028/29; PWLB 5-year currently 4.78%, forecast 4.20%; Bank Rate currently 4%, forecast 3.25%.
findings.quote: The council is currently maintaining an under-borrowed position. This means that the capital borrowing need, (the Capital Financing Requirement), has not been fully funded with loan debt as cash supporting the council's reserves, balances and cash flow has been used as a temporary measure.

findings.headline: £1m from unallocated general fund reserves earmarked for local government reorganisation transition costs
findings.detail: Hart is drawing £1m from its unallocated working balance to fund LGR transition costs: redundancies, TUPE transfers, IT system integration, asset rationalization, and backfilling of seconded staff. This is happening while the council faces a forecast budget deficit ahead, consuming reserves at a time of structural pressure.
findings.matters: Large one-time cost from already-constrained reserves at a moment of financial vulnerability, reducing the council's flexibility to respond to the forecast deficit
findings.figures: £1m from unallocated general fund balance; LGR costs described as 'significant'
findings.quote: It is now essential in setting the budget and MTFS to earmark £1m from the unallocated general fund balance for this purpose.

findings.headline: Core government grant funding declining by £1.2m over the MTFS period
findings.detail: Hart's core government grant is falling from £4,656k (2024/25) to £3,455k (2028/29)—a structural reduction of £1.2m. The council receives transitional funding protection for three years (ending 2028/29), but the new Fair Funding formula delivers substantially lower baseline funding thereafter.
findings.matters: Structural decline in core government funding means the council faces permanent loss of revenue with limited flexibility to recover it
findings.quote: The Government has provided a three-year funding settlement... Transitional funding is provided for 3 years with the 2028/29 fair funding amount being the new funding level

findings.headline: Commercial property income increasingly critical to budget but exposed to void risk
findings.detail: Hart's budget includes £1.17m in investment property rental income. The council acknowledges property is 'an increasingly important revenue stream' but faces risk of rent loss from void periods. CIPFA's Financial Resilience Index identifies Hart as having 'relatively low ratio of income from fees and charges to total service expenditure'—the only higher-risk area identified for the council.
findings.matters: Uncertain, volatile income stream is critical to budget balance; void periods or tenant loss could worsen the forecast deficit
findings.figures: £1.17m investment property rental income; void risk identified as key MTFS risk
findings.quote: Property – this is an increasingly important revenue stream in the Council's budget, so the risk of rent loss due to void periods must be evaluated.

findings.headline: Waste contract cost increased by £1.3m due to statutory weekly food waste requirement, with uncertain government compensation
findings.detail: The Environment Act requires weekly food waste collection. Hart's waste contract cost has increased by £1.3m to implement this mandate. Government promised new burdens funding to cover costs but is not delivering it. The council is using Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) funding—a business tax on waste packaging—to partly cover the cost, but EPR is uncertain and subject to future changes.
findings.matters: A large, non-discretionary cost increase driven by statute has no guaranteed funding, creating operational and financial risk
findings.figures: £1.3m annual waste cost increase; using up to £1m EPR in 2026/27 (uncertain), with £0.5m in revenue budget and balance transferred to contingency reserve
findings.quote: The annual cost of the waste/recycling contract has increased by £1.3m, primarily due to the statutory requirement to implement weekly food waste collections.

findings.headline: £1.5m of promised government funding for new burdens and National Insurance now not delivered
findings.detail: The Council anticipated £1m in new burdens funding for weekly food waste collections and £70k in ongoing National Insurance compensation. These have now been 'theoretically rolled into the overall funding settlement', meaning councils won't receive the promised funding. This creates a recurring structural shortfall.
findings.matters: A £1.5m recurring revenue gap that was promised but not delivered represents a material and permanent loss of income
findings.figures: £1.5m pa compared to 2024/25 budget; £85k net reduction in core grant 2025/26 to 2026/27
findings.quote: Compared to the 2024/25 budget, these two factors alone have increased the Council's costs by £1.5m pa with no specific funding being received as promised.

findings.headline: MTFS forecasts a significant budget shortfall from 2027/28 onwards
findings.detail: While the 2026/27 budget balances, Hart's Medium-Term Financial Strategy shows a 'significant budget shortfall' from 2027/28. This unsustainability is evident in the council already freezing fees (green waste, car parking) and withdrawing reserves for one-off costs, signalling the current position cannot hold.
findings.matters: A forecast deficit makes a council unsellable to lenders and signals imminent need for service reductions or reserves depletion
findings.figures: Core Spending Power declining from £13,775k (2026/27) to £13,687k (2027/28) and £13,581k (2028/29); grant funding drops £388k in 2027/28 and £404k in 2028/29
findings.quote: the MTFS is currently showing a significant budget shortfall in 2027/28 and beyond so reserves will need to be reviewed alongside the budget setting process.

findings.headline: The council is prohibited from borrowing to invest in land or buildings for yield, with PWLB repayment and access penalties for non-compliance.
findings.detail: The strategy explicitly states that restrictions on council borrowing prohibit investments in land or buildings for yield. No yield-based investments are allowed in Hart's capital programme for three years, with no alternative financing options. The council understands that non-compliance will result in repayment of PWLB borrowing and may prevent future access to PWLB.
findings.matters: Lenders to local government need to understand what borrowing options are available to a council and what constraints apply. These PWLB restrictions directly limit Hart's ability to pursue commercial income strategies through capital investments, which affects the council's financial flexibility and revenue options.
findings.figures: three years
findings.quote: Restrictions on council borrowing prohibit investments in land or buildings for yield. No yield-based investments are allowed in the Capital Programme for three years, and no alternative financing options. Non-compliance will result in repayment of PWLB borrowing and may prevent future access to PWLB.
